newsitem.title: USA: Aviron says test to be unblinded in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Aviron says test to be unblinded in 1997.

text.p: Aviron on Monday said Phase III trials of intranasal vaccine for influenza will be unblinded in 1997's third quarter, reducing by one season the amount of time needed to collect test data.
Aviron said the recent winter flu season resulted in sufficient number of culture-confirmed cases of influenza in the test group, thereby allowing the unblinding.

"Although these developments are very unlikely to allow sale of the vaccine sooner than our 1999 target date, the ability to determine the efficacy of this vaccine in children after one year is positive for the company," Chief Executive Officer J. Leighton Read said in a statement.
"We can turn our attention to developing the intranasal vaccine for indications in additional populations, such as healthy adults and those at high risk due to influenza."
The company said clinical investigators remain blinded about which cases of influenza are in the placebo or vaccine group. Efficacy results are expected later in 1997.
Aviron also said it plans a manufacturing consistency trial this spring in 500 children at the Center for Vaccine Development at the University of California, Los Angeles.
